definitions.source: ICAO Doc 9870, Manual on the Prevention of Runway Incursions
definitions.text: Any occurrence at an aerodrome involving the incorrect presence of an aircraft, vehicle or person on the protected area of a surface designated for the landing and takeoff of aircraft.

definitions.source: FAA Runway Safety programme
definitions.text: Runway incursions are classified by cause as pilot deviations, operational incidents (controller actions) or vehicle and pedestrian deviations, and by severity from A to D.

definitions.source: FAA Runway Safety programme
definitions.text: A landing, attempted landing, line-up or takeoff on a surface other than the one assigned: a wrong runway, a taxiway, a closed runway or the wrong airport.

definitions.source: NASA ASRS coding taxonomy
definitions.term: Anomaly: Ground Incursion – Runway or Taxiway
definitions.text: An aircraft, vehicle or person entering a runway or taxiway without authorization, or an aircraft using a taxiway or the wrong runway for landing or takeoff.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – Runway Excursion
definitions.text: An aircraft leaves the runway surface during takeoff or landing, either by veering off the side or by overrunning the end.

definitions.source: ICAO Global Reporting Format (GRF) for runway surface conditions
definitions.text: A runway condition code from 6 (dry) down to 0 reports braking performance on wet or contaminated runways (water, slush, snow, ice), so crews can recompute landing distance.

definitions.source: NASA ASRS coding taxonomy
definitions.text: An aircraft departs the runway surface during the takeoff or landing roll, including overruns after a long or fast landing.

definitions.source: IATA – Loss of Control In-flight (LOC-I)
definitions.text: A significant, unintended departure of the aircraft from controlled flight, such as a stall, spin or upset, often following a system malfunction or crew response to erroneous indications.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – Unreliable Airspeed
definitions.text: Erroneous or disagreeing airspeed indications, for example from pitot icing, ice crystals or a blocked pitot tube, which can lead to an upset if the crew follows the wrong indication.

definitions.source: ICAO Annex 10 – Airborne Collision Avoidance System (ACAS)
definitions.text: An ACAS or TCAS indication to the flight crew recommending a vertical manoeuvre to increase separation from conflicting traffic.

definitions.source: EUROCONTROL – Level bust
definitions.text: An unauthorised vertical deviation of more than 300 feet from the cleared flight level or altitude, a common cause of loss of separation and TCAS resolution advisories.

definitions.source: NASA ASRS coding taxonomy
definitions.text: Two aircraft in flight come into conflict or lose separation, including near midair collisions and TCAS events.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – Clear Air Turbulence
definitions.text: Turbulence in cloud-free air, often near jet streams or over mountains, with no visual cue and often not shown on weather radar.

definitions.source: FAA Advisory Circular 120-88A – Preventing Injuries Caused by Turbulence
definitions.text: Passengers and flight attendants are injured in turbulence mainly when standing or not wearing seat belts, and by unsecured carts and galley equipment.

definitions.source: FAA National Wildlife Strike Database
definitions.text: A collision between an aircraft and a bird or other wildlife, including ingestion into an engine, reported with damage and phase of flight.

definitions.source: 14 CFR 33.76 – Bird ingestion (engine certification)
definitions.text: Engines must be shown to withstand the ingestion of birds of defined sizes; large or multiple bird ingestion can damage fan blades and cause surge, loss of thrust, shutdown or fire.

definitions.source: FAA holdover time guidelines (ground de-icing and anti-icing)
definitions.text: The estimated time a de-icing or anti-icing fluid protects aircraft surfaces from frost or ice; if it is exceeded before takeoff, the aircraft must be checked or de-iced again.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – Hard Landing and Tail Strike
definitions.text: A touchdown with a vertical load above limits, a bounced landing, or contact of the tail with the runway during takeoff rotation or landing flare.

definitions.source: FAA Runway Safety programme
definitions.text: A runway incursion caused by a ground vehicle or a person, such as a driver or pedestrian entering a runway without ATC authorization.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – Crosswind Landings
definitions.text: Landing with a wind component across the runway; strong or gusty crosswinds near the aircraft limit increase the risk of lateral runway excursion (veer-off).

definitions.source: FAA Advisory Circular 120-109A – Stall Prevention and Recovery Training
definitions.text: Training to recognise and recover from approaches to stall and full stalls, including during go-arounds with high thrust and pitch.

definitions.source: FAA Advisory Circular 90-23G – Aircraft Wake Turbulence
definitions.text: Vortices from a preceding aircraft, strongest behind heavy aircraft at slow speed, can cause sudden rolls on approach or departure; spacing reduces the risk.

definitions.source: ICAO Doc 4444 – PANS-ATM (separation minima)
definitions.text: Two aircraft come closer than the prescribed separation minima, often after an ATC clearance or instruction puts them in conflict.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – Hydraulic System Failure
definitions.text: Loss of hydraulic fluid or pressure that degrades flight controls, brakes, steering or landing gear, handled with non-normal checklists.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – Landing Gear Malfunction
definitions.text: Failure of a landing gear leg to extend, retract or lock, requiring alternate extension or a landing with gear not fully down.

definitions.source: 14 CFR 121.354 – Terrain awareness and warning system
definitions.text: Airliners must carry a system that warns the crew of terrain, obstacles and excessive descent so they can climb away before impact.

definitions.source: EASA Safety Information Bulletin 2022-02 – GNSS outages and alterations
definitions.text: Interference with satellite navigation signals, by jamming or spoofing, causes loss of GPS position, false positions or false terrain warnings, especially near conflict zones.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – In-Flight Shutdown
definitions.text: An engine is shut down in flight because of a failure or a precautionary indication such as low oil pressure, high vibration or fire.

definitions.source: FAA Advisory Circular 120-60B – Ground Deicing and Anti-icing Program
definitions.text: No takeoff may be made with frost, ice or snow adhering to wings or control surfaces; contamination must be removed before departure.

definitions.source: ICAO Doc 10117 – Manual on the Legal Aspects of Unruly and Disruptive Passengers
definitions.text: A passenger who fails to respect rules of conduct or to follow crew instructions, disturbing good order and discipline on board.

definitions.source: FAA SAFO – Fire risks from lithium batteries in the cabin
definitions.text: Portable electronic devices and power banks can overheat in thermal runaway, producing smoke and fire in the cabin; crew cool the device with water or non-alcoholic liquid.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – Smoke and Fumes
definitions.text: Smoke, fumes or burning smells in the flight deck or cabin, often electrical in origin, handled with oxygen masks and the smoke checklist.

definitions.source: ICAO Annex 6 – Fuel planning and in-flight fuel management
definitions.text: The crew declares MINIMUM FUEL when any change may land them below final reserve, and MAYDAY FUEL when the landing fuel is expected to be below final reserve.

definitions.source: IATA Ground Operations Manual – Pushback and towing
definitions.text: Moving an aircraft with a tug or towbar, with wing walkers and headset communication, to prevent collisions with aircraft, vehicles and objects.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – Tailstrike
definitions.text: The aft fuselage contacts the runway during takeoff rotation or landing, often after early rotation, wrong takeoff speeds or excessive pitch.

definitions.source: FAA Advisory Circular 00-54 – Pilot Windshear Guide
definitions.text: Sudden changes in wind speed or direction near the ground, such as microbursts from thunderstorms, causing airspeed loss; crews fly the windshear escape manoeuvre.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – Landing Short (Undershoot)
definitions.text: The aircraft touches down before the runway threshold, often after an unstable or low approach or a visual illusion.

definitions.source: FAA Advisory Circular 91-74B – Pilot Guide: Flight in Icing Conditions
definitions.text: Ice accumulates on wings, tail and windshield in supercooled cloud or freezing drizzle, increasing drag and stall speed.

definitions.source: FAA National Wildlife Strike Database – strike reporting
definitions.text: A collision with birds that damages the aircraft, such as a cracked windshield, dented radome or ingested engine, reported to the wildlife strike database.

definitions.source: FAA Runway Safety programme – Pilot deviation
definitions.text: A runway incursion caused by a pilot, such as crossing a hold-short line or entering a runway without an ATC clearance.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – Lateral Navigation Error
definitions.text: The aircraft leaves its cleared route because of a wrong route, waypoint or procedure loaded in the flight management system.

definitions.text: This includes the AIRPROX defined as: A situation in which, in the opinion of a pilot or air traffic services personnel, the distance between aircraft as well as their relative positions and speed have been such that the safety of the aircraft involved may have been compromised. An aircraft proximity is classified as follows: Risk of collision. The risk classification of an aircraft proximity in which serious risk of collision has existed. Safety not assured. The risk classification of an aircraft proximity in which the safety of the aircraft may have been compromised. No risk of collision. The risk classification of an aircraft proximity in which no risk of collision has existed. Risk not determined. The risk classification of an aircraft proximity in which insufficient information was available to determine the risk involved, or inconclusive or conflicting evidence precluded such determination.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 2220600 · Aircraft operation general › Weather encounters
definitions.text: Encounter with any or all of a) clear air turbulence (CAT) b) turbulence in cloud c) vortex / wake turbulence also to be used in events in which the aircraft was damaged by turbulence. CAT: Clear Air Turbulence (CAT) is the bumpiness experienced by aircraft at high altitudes (above 18,000 feet) in either cloud- free conditions or in stratiform clouds. CAT occurs when undulations (known as gravity waves) in the upper atmosphere become steep and unstable, then break down into chaotic motion. The scale of wave motion that normally affects jet aircraft is on the order of ~10 meters to ~1-2 kilometers. These unstable waves occur when vertical wind shear becomes locally excessive, allowing the waves to overcome the stability of environmental temperature conditions. This condition is known as Kelvin-Helmholtz instability. Most CAT occurs on the fringes of (not within the core of) the jet stream, in the vicinity of upper level frontal zones where temperature contrasts are strong. CAT may also occur when strong winds cross a mountain range in certain thermal conditions, allowing gravity waves to amplify and propagate vertically toward the stratosphere. These 'mountain waves' may be smooth undulations, resulting in updrafts and downdrafts (UDDF in pilot report code), or can break down into smaller scale turbulence. A third instance in which CAT occurs is when strong winds encounter the tops of thunderstorm clouds, resulting in strong shear waves that extend well downstream from the convective cloud.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 2220400 · Aircraft operation general › Weather encounters
definitions.text: Wake turbulence: Turbulent air behind an aircraft caused by any of the following: (a) wing-tip vortices; (b) rotor-tip vortices; (c) jet-engine thrust stream or jet blast; (d) rotor downwash; (e) prop wash. Wing tip vortex: A circular pattern of air current created by the movement of an airfoil through the air when the airfoil is generating lift. As an airfoil moves through the atmosphere in sustained flight, an area of high pressure is created beneath it and an area of low pressure is created above it. The air flowing from the high-pressure area to the low-pressure area around and about the tips of the airfoil tends to roll up into two rapidly rotating vortices, cylindrical in shape. These vortices are the predominant parts of aircraft wake turbulence and their rotational force is dependent upon the wing loading, gross weight, and speed of the generating aircraft. The vortices from medium to heavy aircraft can be of extremely high velocity and hazardous to smaller aircraft.

definitions.term: Main gear complete collapse or retraction
definitions.text: An event involving the complete gear collapse or retraction while it was supporting the aircraft.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1322000 · Aircraft/system/component › 3200 Landing gear
definitions.term: Nose/tail landing gear related event (ATA Code:3220)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3220) An event related to the miscellaneous parts of the nose or tail gear system which cannot be directly associated with a specific nose/tail gear code such as attachment, struts or axles. Does not include extension/retraction mechanism, steering/dampening system or doors.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1322001 · Aircraft/system/component › 3200 Landing gear › 3220 Nose/tail landing gear
definitions.text: An event involving the collapse or retraction of the aircraft's nose gear while it was supporting the aircraft.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1324000 · Aircraft/system/component › 3200 Landing gear
definitions.term: Wheels and brakes related event (ATA Code:3240)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3240) An event related to the aircraft's wheels and brakes. Including the brake system miscellaneous parts other than the brake assembly, master cylinder, power valve, anti-skid system, the pressure source and associated system for emergency brake actuation and brake anti-ice system. Typical parts are line, hose, fitting, park brake valve and gauge.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1324100 · Aircraft/system/component › 3200 Landing gear
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3244) An event related to tyre defects and failures.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1324200 · Aircraft/system/component › 3200 Landing gear
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3242) An event involving the parts of the brake unit mounted at the wheels only. Typical parts are disc, cylinder, lining, seal, rotor and housing.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1324207 · Aircraft/system/component › 3200 Landing gear › 3242 Brakes
definitions.text: An event involving the aircraft's parking brake.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1324214 · Aircraft/system/component › 3200 Landing gear › 3242 Brakes
definitions.text: An event involving the aircraft's emergency brake.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1324400 · Aircraft/system/component › 3200 Landing gear
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3241) An event involving the system units and parts which automatically control brake pressure during landing roll to prevent tyre skidding. Typical parts are transducer, control box and valve.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1325000 · Aircraft/system/component › 3200 Landing gear
definitions.term: Landing gear steering related event (ATA Code:3250)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3250) An event involving the miscellaneous system parts other than the actuator which provide for aircraft directional control on the ground. Includes main gear steering systems. Does not include wheel braking systems. Typical parts are, cable, rod end, collar, line, valve and accumulator.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1326000 · Aircraft/system/component › 3200 Landing gear
definitions.term: Landing gear position and warning system related event (ATA Code:3260)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3260) An event involving the system parts which provide indication and warning of the landing gear position. Includes gear safety switches which prevent inadvertent actuation such as squat or air/ground sensor. Typical parts are relay, switch bracket, lamp, horn, up lock switch, down lock switch and in transit switch.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1327000 · Aircraft/system/component › 3200 Landing gear
definitions.term: Auxiliary landing gear related event (ATA Code:3270)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3270) An event involving the devices such as tail skids on tricycle gear aircraft used to stabilize the aircraft on the ground and to prevent ground contact damage. This code is also used for supplementary wheels on rotorcraft, skids for ground handling but not for skids or amphibian/seaplane floats, hull or associated retractable landing gear. Does not include auxiliary or emergency landing gear extension systems.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1327001 · Aircraft/system/component › 3200 Landing gear › 3270 Auxiliary landing gear
definitions.text: An event involving the collapse or retraction of gear other than the nose, tail or main gear, while it is supporting the weight of the aircraft.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1330000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3300) An event involving the units and components which provide for external and internal illumination. Includes light fixtures, switches and wiring. Does not include warning lights for individual systems.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1340000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3400) An event involving the units and components which provide aircraft navigational information.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010018 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems
definitions.term: 3410 Flight Environment Data systems realeted event
definitions.text: Events related to that portion of the system which senses environmental conditions and uses the data to influence navigation. Includes such items as Central Air Data Computers, pitot/static systems, air temperature, rate-of-climb, airspeed, high speed warning, altitude, altitude reporting, altimeter correction system, air disturbance detection system, etc.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1341400 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems › 3410 Flight Environment Data
definitions.term: Airspeed/Mach indicating system related event (ATA Code:3414)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3414) An event involving the instrument which measures and indicates speed of the aircraft.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1341600 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems › 3410 Flight Environment Data
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3416) An event involving the altimeters and barometric encoders used to measure and indicate altitude. Also includes the unit which senses and alerts to a change in a pre-selected altitude. Does not include the ground proximity systems. Typical parts are dial, case, pointer and spring.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010069 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems › 3410 Flight Environment Data
definitions.term: Flight management system related event (ATA Code:3418)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3418) An event involving the system which combines navigational data to compute or manage the aircraft's geographical position or theoretical flight path. Typical parts are course computers, flight management computers, performance data computers, associated control display units and warning annunciators.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1342000 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems
definitions.term: 3420 Attitude and direction data system related event (ATA Code:3420)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3420) An event involving the system components and parts which use magnetic, gyroscopic, and inertia forces to indicate an aircraft attitude and direction. Includes such items as the inertial reference system (IRS).

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1343000 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems
definitions.term: Landing and taxi aids related event (ATA Code:3430)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3430) An event involving the system providing guidance during approach, landing and taxiing. Includes such items as, ILS, paravisual director, ground guidance systems and markers.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1344000 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems
definitions.term: Independent position determining system related event (ATA Code:3440)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3440) An event involving the system which provides information to determine the aircraft's position and is primarily independent of ground installations. Typical parts are star tracker and sextants/octants.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1344400 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems › 3440 Independent position system
definitions.term: Ground proximity warning system related event (ATA Code:3444)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3444) An event involving the system which detects and alerts flight crew to potential terrain hazards. Includes the antenna which transmits and receives an electronic signal for the radio altimeter equipment used for terrain-to-aircraft distance. Also includes the component which interprets a radio signal reflected back to a receiver to determine distance from the nearest terrain; and the component which process the warning computer input signals from various sources in order to determine if and when the crew should be alerted of a terrain hazard.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1344401 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems › 3440 Independent position system › 3444 Ground proximity warning
definitions.term: Ground proximity warning system nuisance alarm
definitions.text: An event involving nuisance warnings by the aircraft's ground proximity warning system.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1344402 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems › 3440 Independent position system › 3444 Ground proximity warning
definitions.term: Other ground proximity warning system related event
definitions.text: An event involving the aircraft's ground proximity warning system other than a nuisance warning.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1344500 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems › 3440 Independent position system
definitions.term: Airborne collision avoidance system/traffic alert and collision avoidance system related
definitions.text: event (ATA Code:3445) (3445 ACAS/TCAS) (ATA Code:3445) An event involving the system which provides information to determine aircraft position and is primarily independent of ground installations (i.e., traffic alert and collision avoidance system TCAS). Typical parts are collision avoidance monitoring units.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1344501 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems › 3440 Independent position system › Airborne collision avoidance system/traffic alert and collision avoidance system related
definitions.text: An event involving a nuisance alarm from the aircraft's airborne collision avoidance system or traffic alert and collision avoidance system.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010019 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems
definitions.term: 3450 Dependent Position Determining System related event
definitions.text: Events related to that portion of the system which provides information to determine position and is mainly dependent on ground installations or orbital satellites. Includes items such as DME, transponders, radio compass, LORAN, VOR, ADF, OMEGA, GLOBAL POSITIONING, etc.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1341800 · Aircraft/system/component › 3400 Navigation systems
definitions.term: Flight management system related event (ATA Code:3460)
definitions.text: An event involving the system which combines navigational data to compute or manage the aircraft's geographical position or theoretical flight path. Typical parts are course computers, flight management computers, performance data computers, associated control display units and warning annunciators.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1350000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3500) An event involving the units and components which store, regulate and deliver breathing oxygen to the passengers and crew. Typical parts are bottles, relief valves, shut-off valves, outlets, regulators, masks and walk-around bottles.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1360000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3600) An event involving the units and components which deliver large volumes of compressed air from a power source to connecting points for other systems such as air conditioning, pressurization and de-icing.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1370000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3700) An event involving the units and components used to generate, deliver and regulate negative air pressure.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1380000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.term: Drinkable/waste water system related event (ATA Code:3800)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:3800) An event involving the fixed units and components which store and deliver fresh water. Also includes those fixed components which store and furnish a means of removal of water and waste.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010020 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: Event related to units and components provided for the storage, balancing, control, filling, discharge, and dumping of water ballast.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010021 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: Event related to computing devices that can host software applications for system functions that had traditionally been implemented in dedicated hardware. The actual system functions are covered in their respective ATA chapters.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010022 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: Event related to units and components which furnish a means of entertaining the passengers and providing communication within the aircraft and between the aircraft cabin and ground stations. Includes voice, data, music and video transmissions. Does not include SATCOM, HF, VHF, UHF and all transmitting/receiving equipment, antennas, etc., which are covered in Chapter 23 or Chapter 46.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010023 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: Event related to units, components and associated system which interfaces with multiple aircraft systems. Contains checkout and fault isolation procedures using a central computer complex and/or standard fault isolation procedures to locate a single system or component malfunction.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010024 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: Event related to units and components which furnish a means of storing, updating, and retrieving digital information traditionally provided on paper, microfilm, or microfiche. Includes units that are dedicated to the information storage and retrieval function such as the Electronic Library mass storage and controller. Does not include units or components installed for other uses and shared with other systems, such as flight deck printer or general use display.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010025 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: Event relted to units and components used to generate, store, deliver and regulate inert gas. Includes regulators, lines, manifolds, etc.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1490000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.term: Auxiliary power unit related event (ATA Code:4900)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:4900) An event involving the airborne auxiliary power units (APU) installed on aircraft for the purpose of generating and supplying a single type or combination of auxiliary electric, hydraulic, pneumatic or other power. Does not include generators, alternators, hydraulic pumps or their connecting systems which supply and deliver power to their respective aircraft systems.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1255000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.term: 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments related events
definitions.text: Those compartments for storage of cargo and various components and accessories. Includes those systems used to load/unload cargo and other cargo related systems. Does not include aircraft structure which is in Capter 53

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010007 · Aircraft/system/component › 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments
definitions.text: Event related to compartments for the storage of cargo

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1255900 · Aircraft/system/component › 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments › 5010 Cargo Compartments
definitions.text: An event involving the aircraft's cargo.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1255901 · Aircraft/system/component › 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments › 5010 Cargo Compartments › 5019 Cargo related
definitions.text: An event involving a leak from the aircraft's cargo other than a radiation leak.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1255902 · Aircraft/system/component › 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments › 5010 Cargo Compartments › 5019 Cargo related
definitions.text: An event involving a shift of the aircraft's cargo after the aircraft was loaded.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1255903 · Aircraft/system/component › 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments › 5010 Cargo Compartments › 5019 Cargo related
definitions.text: An event involving smoke, fumes or fire in the aircraft's cargo compartment.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1255904 · Aircraft/system/component › 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments › 5010 Cargo Compartments › 5019 Cargo related
definitions.text: An event involving a leak of radioactive material, or radiation, from the aircraft's cargo.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1255905 · Aircraft/system/component › 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments › 5010 Cargo Compartments › 5019 Cargo related
definitions.text: Cargo/sling load dropped: to used when the dropping of the load was the rwsult of any failure. Intentional dropping of the sling load is covered under 'consequential events'

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010008 · Aircraft/system/component › 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments
definitions.text: Events related to systems which have components which are or can be mounted on the aircraft and used to load/unload, restrain, guide or service cargo. Includes drive systems, rollers, latches, restraint nets etc.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010009 · Aircraft/system/component › 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments
definitions.text: Events related to systems which are related to loading/unloading of cargo. Includes aircraft levelling, loader alignment systems etc. Does not include Cargo Loading Systems.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010011 · Aircraft/system/component › 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments
definitions.text: Event related to compartments used for the housing of various components and accessories. Includes wheel wells, tail- hydraulic-electrical/electronic equipment racks, main battery structure etc.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010012 · Aircraft/system/component › 5000 Cargo and accessory compartments
definitions.text: Events related to insulation blankets which are used for heat and sound insulation. Includes cargo compartments and accessory compartments, insulation, etc.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1510000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5100) An event involving the standard practices and general procedures for typical repairs applicable to the aircraft's airframe or structure.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1510100 · Aircraft/system/component › 5100 Standard practices and structures
definitions.term: Airframe structure - general related event (ATA Code:5101)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5101) An event involving aircraft structural problems of a general nature which affects two or more areas. Includes reports of lightning strikes which cannot be associated with a specific code.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1520000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5200) An event involving any of the removable units used for entrance or exit and for enclosing other structure contained within the fuselage. Includes passenger and crew doors, cargo doors and emergency exits. Electrical and hydraulic systems associated with door control are included as appropriate.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1520100 · Aircraft/system/component › 5200 Aircraft's doors
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5201) An event involving any of the aircraft's doors in general.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1520101 · Aircraft/system/component › 5200 Aircraft's doors › 5201 Doors - general
definitions.text: An event involving the inadvertent or intentional opening of any of the aircraft's doors.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1520102 · Aircraft/system/component › 5200 Aircraft's doors › 5201 Doors - general
definitions.text: An event involving the separation of any of the aircraft's doors.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1520170 · Aircraft/system/component › 5200 Aircraft's doors › 5201 Doors - general
definitions.text: An event involving the aircraft's door warning system.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1530000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.term: Aircraft's fuselage structure related event (ATA Code:5300)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5300) An event involving the structural units and associated components and members which make up the compartments for crew, passengers, equipment, cargo and the structure of the envelope and gondola of airships.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1530100 · Aircraft/system/component › 5300 Aircraft's fuselage structure
definitions.term: Airframe failure - other than general breakup (ATA Code:5301)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5301) An event involving a failure of the aircraft's airframe or structure other than a general disintegration or break-up.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1530200 · Aircraft/system/component › 5300 Aircraft's fuselage structure
definitions.term: Airframe general disintegration or break-up (ATA Code:5302)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5302) An event involving a general disintegration or break-up of the aircraft's airframe or structure.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1540000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.term: Aircraft engine nacelle or pylon structure related event (ATA Code:5400)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5400) An event involving the structural units and associated components and members which furnish a means of mounting and housing the power plant or rotor assembly. Includes the structure of power plant cowling inclusive of the structural portion of the inlet whether or not integral with the aircraft. Structural portions of the exhaust system are excluded where they are not integral with the airframe.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1550000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.term: Aircraft empennage stucture related event (ATA Code:5500)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5500) An event involving the horizontal and vertical stabilizers including the structure of the elevator and rudder. This code is also used for reports that pertain to flying wires.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010026 · Aircraft/system/component › 5500 Aircraft empennage structure
definitions.text: Event related to the horizontal airfoil of the tail or nose section to which the elevator is attached. Includes items such as spars, ribs, stringers, skins, access covers, tips, attach/attached fittings, etc.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1552000 · Aircraft/system/component › 5500 Aircraft empennage structure
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5520) An event involving the structural aspects of the movable aerofoil hinged to the horizontal stabilizer for longitudinal control. Includes the 'ruddervator' on V-tail aircraft and balance weights. Does not include the stabilator structure.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010027 · Aircraft/system/component › 5500 Aircraft empennage structure
definitions.text: Event related to the vertical airfoil to which the rudder is attached. Includes items such as spars, ribs, stringers, skins, access covers, tips, attach/attached fittings, etc.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1554000 · Aircraft/system/component › 5500 Aircraft empennage structure
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5540) An event involving the structural aspects of the vertical aerofoil hinged to the vertical stabilizer. Does not include the actuators, actuator mechanism or mounting. Typical parts are hinge, hinge fittings, bearing, bolt and miscellaneous structure.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1560000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5600) An event involving the fuselage and crew compartment windows inclusive of windshields.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1560100 · Aircraft/system/component › 5600 Aircraft windows/windshields
definitions.term: Aircraft's windows in general related event (ATA Code:5601)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5601) An event involving the aircraft's windows in general.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1560101 · Aircraft/system/component › 5600 Aircraft windows/windshields › 5601 Aircraft's windows in general
definitions.text: An event involving the separation in flight of an aircraft window.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1561000 · Aircraft/system/component › 5600 Aircraft windows/windshields
definitions.text: 5610 Flight compartment window: includes cockpit windows, cockpit overhead canopies, observation windows, and windshield panels in the flight compartment. Includes attachment and sliding feature of sliding windows. For cockpit windows including the breakage of electrically heated windshield panels regardless of cause.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1570000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.term: Aircraft wing structure related event (ATA Code:5700)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:5700) An event involving the centre wing and outer wing structural units and associated components and members which support the aircraft in flight. This code should be used for general reports of the primary wing structure. Control surfaces (on the wing) related event (ATA Code:5750) (5750 Control surfaces)                                    1575000   * (ATA Code:5750) An event involving the control surfaces which are attached to the wing.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010028 · Aircraft/system/component › 5700 Aircraft wing structure
definitions.term: 5740 Wing Leading Edge and Leading Edge Devices
definitions.text: Event related to skins and structure of the wing leading edge and removable leading edge airfoils such as flaps, slats, attach/attached fittings, etc.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010029 · Aircraft/system/component › 5700 Aircraft wing structure
definitions.term: 5750 Wing Trailing Edge / Trailing Edge Devices
definitions.text: Event related to skins and structure of the wing and trailing edge and removable edge airfoils such as flaps and attach/attached fittings

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 99010076 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: (ATA Code 6000) STANDARD PRACTICES - PROPELLER/ROTOR

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1610000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.text: (ATA Code:6100) An event involving the complete mechanical or electrical propeller, governor, alternators, pumps, motors those units and components external to or integral with the engine used to control the propeller blade angle. Includes the propulsor duct assemblies, aerodynamic fairing of mechanical components, stators and vectoring systems.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1610100 · Aircraft/system/component › 6100 Propellers generally
definitions.text: (ATA Code:6101) An event involving any of the aircraft's propellers in general.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1610101 · Aircraft/system/component › 6100 Propellers generally › 6101 Aircraft propellers - general
definitions.text: An event involving a propeller over-speed.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1610102 · Aircraft/system/component › 6100 Propellers generally › 6101 Aircraft propellers - general
definitions.text: An event involving the separation of a propeller from its engine.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1610120 · Aircraft/system/component › 6100 Propellers generally › 6101 Aircraft propellers - general
definitions.text: An event related to the control of a propeller.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1620000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.term: Rotorcraft main rotor systems related event (ATA Code:6200)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:6200) An event involving the rotorcraft main rotor systems. Main rotor: the rotor that supplies the principal lift to a rotorcraft.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1620100 · Aircraft/system/component › 6200 Rotorcraft main rotor system
definitions.term: Helicopter's main rotor in general related event (ATA Code:6201)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:6201) An event involving a helicopter's main rotor in general. Main rotor: the rotor that supplies the principal lift to a rotorcraft.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1620101 · Aircraft/system/component › 6200 Rotorcraft main rotor system › 6201 Main rotor - general
definitions.text: An event involving flapping of the helicopter's main rotor blades.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1630000 · Aircraft/system/component
definitions.term: Main rotor drive system related event (ATA Code:6300)
definitions.text: (ATA Code:6300) An event involving the main rotor drive system.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1630100 · Aircraft/system/component › 6300 Main rotor drive system
definitions.text: (ATA Code:6301) An event involving the helicopter's main rotor drive shaft.

definitions.source: ECCAIRS 1.3.0.12 · Events (390) · 1632000 · Aircraft/system/component › 6300 Main rotor drive system
definitions.text: (ATA Code:6320) An event involving the component which transmits engine power to rotary motion in the main rotor mast.
